_comment: Template for `create-clients-cosmos --l2-config` on OPTIMISM. Copy to
op-l2-config.json (gitignored) and fill in your deployment's values.
The values below are OP SEPOLIA, so they are real and checkable. For the local
devnet (run_optimism_node.sh) use l2_chain_id 2151908 and the router address
deploy_l2_contracts.sh printed. Its checked-in public key matches the local
attestor handoff; replace it with your own attestor public key on every other network.
rollup_profile is submitted verbatim in MsgCreateClient and the Rust verifier
rejects unknown fields, so common carries exactly these five keys — no
ethereum_client, no dispute_game_factory, no game_list_slot, no finality_policy.
The attestor-trusted client verifies nothing against L1.
Four fields must be right or the client fails, each in its own way:
profile_version  must match the wasm artifact (op_attestor_v1 /
base_attestor_v1 / arbitrum_attestor_v1) — a mismatch fails
at instantiate with InvalidProfileVersion.
l2_header_fork   must match the chain's execution-header layout. OP Stack
keeps the L1 header shape, so prague; Arbitrum Nitro emits
none of the post-London optional fields and needs london.
A mismatch is rejected on EVERY update, not at creation.
l2_chain_id      must be the chain the relayer's l2_rpc_url actually serves.
Both `create-clients-cosmos --l2-config` and `start` verify it
against eth_chainId and refuse to proceed on a mismatch; the
create path also refuses when the endpoint does not answer,
because it is about to commit the profile on-chain.
Nothing else reads the field: transactions take their chain id
from the RPC, so before these checks a wrong value relayed
happily against whatever chain the URL served.
wasm_checksum is printed by scripts/local/wasm_op.sh, and is the sha256 of the
UNCOMPRESSED wasm. counterparty_client_id is the client id on the L2 router
that tracks Cosmos; create-clients-eth registers the SpectreClient under it.
wasm_checksum: <hex checksum from `gaiad q ibc-wasm checksums`, e.g. a49e97b0...>
